The proposed solution claims that the Schur square of the HRS code has dimension \(t\).  However, known results for the Schur product of hyper‑derivative Reed–Solomon codes state that, under the given parameter constraints (\(p\ge t\ge 2s\) and \(t\le\frac{r+2s-1}{2}\)), the dimension of the Schur square is actually  

\[
\dim(C^{\star 2}) = 2t - 2s + 1,
\]

which for the special case \(s=1\) reduces to the classical Reed–Solomon result \(\min\{n,2t-1\}\).  The answer “\(t\)” does not match this formula, so the final answer is incorrect.  

VERDICT: REJECT (the final answer is not correct)
